title_zh: Los Altos、Mountain View 与 Palo Alto 卖房准备：修缮与布置报价怎么比较？
title_en: Preparing to Sell in Los Altos, Mountain View, or Palo Alto: Comparing Repair and Staging Quotes
summary_zh: 同样写着“卖房前准备”，报价里的工作可能很不一样。把范围、材料、时间和额外费用逐项对齐，再决定哪些投入适合你的销售计划。
summary_en: Two pre-sale preparation quotes may cover very different work. Align scope, materials, timing, and additional charges before deciding which investments fit your selling plan.
body_zh:
准备在 Los Altos、Mountain View 或 Palo Alto 卖房时，业主可能同时收到油漆、修缮、清洁和家具布置的报价。总金额很容易比较，真正需要花时间看的，是每份报价到底包含了什么。

这篇清单关注“怎样比较报价”，帮助你把准备计划说清楚，再与具体供应商确认。

一、先把需求写成同一份说明
列出准备处理的房间、项目和希望达到的状态。比如墙面处理，要说清楚哪些位置、是否包含修补、谁负责搬动和保护家具。向不同供应商提供同一份说明，并请对方标注无法确认或需要现场查看的部分。

涉及承包施工时，加州承包商执照管理局建议取得至少三份书面报价，并基于相同的图纸、规格与工作范围进行比较；也可从其官网核对承包商执照状态。这里的承包施工指引，不应直接套用为所有布置服务的执照要求。
官方参考：https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Consumers/Hire_A_Contractor/Finding_The_Right_Contractor.aspx

二、把“包含”与“另外收费”并排看
可以为每项工作留四栏：包含的内容、未包含的内容、尚待确认的条件、计费方式。遇到“视情况”“基本处理”等模糊表述，先请对方补充解释。

例如，家具布置可以询问运输、安装、撤场、租用期限和延期费用；清洁可以询问窗户、车库或施工后清理是否在范围内。这些是用来提问的项目，不代表每份报价都会包含。

三、把工期放进整个上市时间表
让修缮完成、清洁、布置、摄影与上市准备的先后关系清楚可见。分别记录预计日期、已经确认的日期，以及会影响下一步的事项。材料待定或进场条件尚未落实时，保留为待确认，不把预计完工日当作已经保证的结果。

四、弄清楚变更怎样确认
对承包施工，CSLB 的家装合同说明强调：价格或工作范围变更，应在变更前由客户与承包商签署书面变更单。具体合同与适用要求请查看官方说明。
官方参考：https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Consumers/Hire_A_Contractor/Home_Improvement_Contracts/what_is_a_contract.aspx

对其他服务，也可以在委托前问清新增项目、延期与取消怎样记录和计费。有新增想法时，先了解费用和时间影响，再决定是否同意。

五、让每项投入对应一个明确目的
这项工作是在处理房屋状况问题，还是帮助买家理解空间？如果暂时不做，会留下什么具体问题？能否先请专业人员评估，再决定范围？把问题写下来，比单看报价总额更容易讨论取舍。

房屋准备需要结合实际状况、时间和预算。某项投入的成交价格影响，不能仅凭供应商报价或别人的经历确定。

CiCi 可以与你一起梳理销售准备优先级和待确认事项，专业施工与合同问题由相应人员确认。用心服务每一个家，让每一次交易、每一分投入，都创造更大的价值。

body_en:
When preparing a home for sale in Los Altos, Mountain View, or Palo Alto, you may receive separate quotes for painting, repairs, cleaning, and furniture staging. The totals are easy to compare. Understanding the work behind each total takes a closer look.

Use this checklist to organize your questions before choosing providers.

1. Give each provider the same brief
List the rooms, tasks, and intended result. For painting, for example, identify the surfaces, ask whether patching is included, and clarify who moves and protects furniture. Share the same brief with each provider and ask them to identify uncertainties or items requiring a site visit.

For contracted construction work, California’s Contractors State License Board recommends obtaining at least three written bids based on the same plans, specifications, and scope. Its website also provides a contractor license check. This construction guidance should not be treated as a blanket licensing requirement for every staging service.
Official reference:
https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Consumers/Hire_A_Contractor/Finding_The_Right_Contractor.aspx

2. Compare inclusions and additional charges
For each task, create four columns: included work, exclusions, unresolved conditions, and pricing method. Ask providers to explain vague descriptions before you rely on them.

For staging, useful questions include delivery, installation, removal, rental duration, and extension charges. For cleaning, ask whether windows, the garage, or post-construction cleanup are included. These are prompts for clarification, rather than assumptions about what a particular quote covers.

3. Connect the work to the listing schedule
Map the sequence of repairs, cleaning, staging, photography, and listing preparation. Distinguish estimated dates from confirmed arrangements and note dependencies. If materials or site access remain unresolved, keep those items visible rather than treating an estimated finish date as a guaranteed outcome.

4. Clarify how changes are approved
For construction contracts, CSLB’s home-improvement guidance says changes to price or scope should be documented in a written change order signed by the customer and contractor before the change. Consult its official guidance for the relevant contract requirements.
Official reference:
https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Consumers/Hire_A_Contractor/Home_Improvement_Contracts/what_is_a_contract.aspx

For other services, ask how added work, extensions, and cancellations will be recorded and charged before engaging the provider. When a new idea arises, understand its cost and timing before agreeing to proceed.

5. Give each investment a purpose
Does the work address a condition issue or help buyers understand a room? What specific concern remains if you defer it? Would a professional assessment help define the scope first? These questions make tradeoffs easier to discuss than the total alone.

Preparation should reflect the home’s condition, your timing, and your budget. A quote or another owner’s experience cannot establish how a particular improvement will affect your eventual sale price.

CiCi can help organize preparation priorities and questions for your providers. Construction and contract matters should be confirmed with the appropriate professionals. Thoughtful care for every home means helping every transaction and every investment create greater value.
